metadata.title: Dependency Transparency (SBOM)

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for achieving transparency into third‑party software dependencies without asserting trust, safety, or authorization.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Software composition analysis, SBOM generation, dependency inventories, and vulnerability correlation tooling.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Solution pattern providing dependency visibility as a prerequisite for supply‑chain risk assessment.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines SBOMs, dependency graphs, component metadata, and vulnerability mappings as trust‑relevant data.

props.name: nist-controls
props.remarks: Dependency Transparency supports supply‑chain risk awareness and vulnerability assessment.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices.

metadata.remarks: Dependency Transparency provides visibility into third‑party and open‑source software composition. Transparency alone does not imply trust, approval, safety, or permission to deploy or execute.

components.title: SBOM Generation
components.description: Generates software bills of materials representing direct and transitive dependencies for SDLC artifacts.

techniques.name: Software Bill of Materials
techniques.remarks: Creation of standardized inventories of software components.

components.title: Dependency Inventory and Mapping
components.description: Maintains an inventory of open‑source and third‑party components, including versioning and transitive relationships.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.remarks: Insertion of malicious or vulnerable dependencies into software compositions.

techniques.name: Dependency Analysis
techniques.remarks: Analysis of dependency trees to identify risk exposure.

components.title: Vulnerability Correlation
components.description: Correlates dependency inventories with known vulnerability data sources.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.remarks: Exploitation of vulnerable dependencies once deployed.

techniques.name: Vulnerability Identification
techniques.remarks: Identification of known vulnerabilities affecting dependencies.

components.title: Dependency Transparency Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Defines what dependency transparency does not grant or imply.
components.remarks: The presence of an SBOM, dependency inventory, or vulnerability mapping does not imply trust, approval, deployability, safety, or runtime authorization.
